newsitem.title: USA: NYSEG completes natgas storage project.
newsitem.headline: NYSEG completes natgas storage project.

text.p: New York State Electric & Gas Corp said Friday it has completed the first high deliverable natural gas storage facility in the northeastern United States.

Located near Watkins Glen, N.Y., the Seneca Lake Storage Project was built at a cost of $57.1 million. It is NYSEG's first storage operation, and signals the utility's intent to become one of the dominant natural gas distribution companies in the northeast, the company said.
The project is funded under NYSEG's three-year gas rate price cap, it noted.

The project will supplement NYSEG's natural gas supply to those markets served by the Columbia Gas System Inc and Consolidated Natural Gas Co Transmission systems, and removes supply constraints during the heating season caused by Columbia's limited pipeline capacity.

The storage facility includes a solution mined salt cavern storage with an 800 million cubic feet working gas capacity. Its compressor station is capable of delivering 80 million cubic feet of natural gas a day..
The facility is connected through a 20-mile pipeline to the CNG Transmission System at Big Flats.
NYSEG said it is constructing a 35-mile pipeline, scheduled to be completed December 1, that will connect the Binghamton area to the CNG system near Ithaca.
